scope: Every public Hugging Face model repo that is a derivative of Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B

constraints_honoured.weight_files_downloaded: none — only JSON metadata, model cards, safetensors index files and HTTP Range reads of safetensors JSON headers

method.transport: Hugging Face HTTP API over urllib, authenticated as user 'malaiwah' with the token at /var/tmp/hf-home-3/token (write-scope token, used read-only). All public repos also resolve unauthenticated.
endpoints_used: GET /api/models/{id}?blobs=true — repo metadata + sibling file list with sizes
HTTP Range GET on model.safetensors: bytes 0-7 for the header length, then the JSON header — tensor names only, no tensor payload
search_queries: search=Qwen3.8 <fmt> for fmt in nvfp4 fp8 awq gptq exl3 exl2 gguf mlx int4 w4a16 compressed-tensors bnb quanto ik_llama mxfp4 autoround coreml openvino onnx w8a8 fp4
method.filter_rule: keep if (id contains '27b' AND id matches /qwen[-_]?3[._]8/) OR tags contain 'qwen3.8-27b'. Drops the other Qwen3.8 sizes (2.4T-A95B, 1.0B-A0.6B, ...).
method.detail_selection_rule: fetch full detail when the repo has a focus quant format (nvfp4/fp4/exl3/exl2/compressed-tensors/w4a16/w4a8/awq/gptq/autoround/int4/fp8/mxfp4/mxfp8) OR the author is on the credible-quanter list OR downloads >= 1000 OR likes >= 5 OR (created >= 2026-08-15 AND downloads >= 100); plus an explicit must-fetch list. Thireus SPECIAL_SPLIT shard repos collapsed to one representative (126 sibling repos, one per quant type).
method.readme_coverage: model cards fetched for every one of the 952 candidates: 464 in the detailed set, the remaining 488 as README-only for the citation sweep.
known_gaps: Full-text search on huggingface.co is fuzzy and token-based; a card that references us only in an image or an external link would not be found.

Repos whose weights live on non-main branches are only fully inventoried for turboderp/Qwen3.8-27B-exl3 and Minachist/Qwen3.8-27B-INT8-AutoRound; for others, usedStorage exceeding HEAD bytes reflects superseded revisions, not extra content.
GGUF internal metadata (per-tensor quant types) was not read; GGUF classification relies on filenames and model cards.
Download counts are HF's 30-day rolling figure at scan time, not lifetime.

unsloth_question.question: Did unsloth update its NVFP4 quant of Qwen3.8-27B since we pinned it, and is it still the NVFP4 of record?
unsloth_question.verdict: NO RECONVERSION. Both weight blobs at HEAD are byte-identical to our pin. What happened was a history super-squash plus metadata edits. Our published number describes the artifact unsloth is serving right now.
unsloth_question.answered_by: sha256 comparison via paths-info, not by reading the commit list

digest_comparison.note: matches the HEAD digest already recorded against our pin; the reviewed tokenizer silently truncates at 2,048 tokens through the raw tokenizers API

independent_corroborations.finding: carries exactly c473512c... and 1d8268aa..., so the pinned-era and HEAD weight blobs are provably the same objects under two revision ids

independent_corroborations.kind: unrelated third party carrying the pre-squash metadata

all three carry both unsloth digests unchanged, independently confirming there is only one set of NVFP4 weights in circulation under this name

config_delta_at_head.quantization_config.config_groups.group_: KEY ABSENT at HEAD. Our pin had 'imatrix_mse'. The contract recorded HEAD as null; the config.json the API serves omits the key entirely rather than setting it null.
config_delta_at_head.group_0: float-quantized W8A8, channel weights / dynamic per-token activations, targets self_attn.{q,k,v,o}_proj, linear_attn.{in_proj_qkv,in_proj_z,out_proj}, lm_head, and layers 56-63 MLP
config_delta_at_head.group_1: nvfp4-pack-quantized W4A4, tensor_group strategy, group_size 16, FP8 E4M3 scales, targets mlp.{gate,up,down}_proj

does_our_published_number_describe_a_sup.reasoning: Mean KLD 0.031059 [0.027916, 0.034795] with 92.90% top-1 over 10,480,640 scored v5 positions, and the 21.34 GiB measured resident weight, were all measured against blobs c473512c... and 1d8268aa..., which are exactly what unsloth serves at revision 16b6615a today. Nothing about the model changed. The only live risk is that a reader downloading HEAD gets the replacement tokenizer.json (06b95093...), which changes tokenisation, not weights.

still_the_nvfp4_of_record.answer: Yes by adoption, no longer unchallenged on merit.
still_the_nvfp4_of_record.adoption: 276,269 downloads / 185 likes, roughly 2.9x the next NVFP4 (RadixArk 96,972) and 5.4x Inferact (51,350).
challengers: gittensor-model-hub/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4-RTX5090 (19.20 GiB ModelOpt W4A4) publishes a head-to-head against unsloth on a 5090 claiming 18.8 vs 22.7 GB resident, 275,941 vs 77,184-token FP8 KV pool, 80.6 vs 42.4 tok/s decode and native 256k where unsloth caps near 77k, with accuracy tied 45/60 on a 20-item smoke.

rdtand/Qwen3.8-27B-PrismaAQUA-5.5bit-vllm (22.00 GiB) is a per-Linear error-priced mixed-precision build that publishes an actual KL protocol.

nm-testing/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4-FP8, created 2026-08-16 with an empty card, reproduces unsloth's exact mixed NVFP4+FP8 recipe with compressed-tensors 0.18.1 and ships unsloth's exact model_mtp.safetensors blob — Red Hat / Neural Magic appears to be staging an official release.
still_the_nvfp4_of_record.note: No competitor has published a KLD measured on a corpus anywhere near our 10.48 M positions; the largest external protocol found is chriswritescode's 278,392 positions, and that one is our own v3 suite.

citations_of_our_work.excerpt:
ributional fidelity to BF16, not task accuracy. **No public
task benchmark has been run** on this checkpoint. Absolute KLD magnitudes are
suite-specific; the paired comparison against official FP8 on identical contexts
is the transferable result.

Corpus, BF16 reference captures, shared LM head and harness come from
[`malaiwah/qwen38-27b-fidelity-suite-v3`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/malaiwah/qwen38-27b-fidelity-suite-v3)
and [`malaiwah/qwen38-27b-exl3`](https://github.com/malaiwah/qwen38-27b-exl3)
(`tools/fidelity.py`), used unmodified.

axes_we_defend: native 262,144-token context on a single 32 GB card
low KLD to BF16 on a large held-out corpus
shortlist_to_measure.ordered_by: what measuring it would tell us, most informative first

plausibly_competitive_unmeasured.why: It is the only repo in the landscape that attacks our headline claim directly and by name: full 262,144 context on one 32 GB RTX 5090, with a published head-to-head against unsloth NVFP4 (18.8 vs 22.7 GB resident, 275,941 vs 77,184-token FP8 KV pool, 80.6 vs 42.4 tok/s, longest completed prompt 242,686 tokens). Vision tower and all 15 MTP tensors are in the file. 52 likes on 1,414 downloads is unusually high conviction.
plausibly_competitive_unmeasured.what_must_be_measured: Mean KLD and top-1 on v5 (10,480,640 positions) against BF16, paired per context. Then the two things its own card does not settle: (a) whether its FP8 KV cache with baked scales is what buys the 275k pool, in which case the comparison against unsloth-without-FP8-KV is not like-for-like and we should re-run unsloth with --kv-cache-dtype fp8; (b) whether MTP actually drafts, since the tensors are present but the recipe leaves them BF16 and the serve command never enables speculative decoding.
plausibly_competitive_unmeasured.what_it_would_tell_us: Whether uniform ModelOpt W4A4 at 19.2 GiB is genuinely on the Pareto frontier we claim, or whether its 20-item smoke is hiding a fidelity gap that a 10 M-position KLD would expose. This is the single highest-value measurement in the list.
plausibly_competitive_unmeasured.cost_note: 19.20 GiB download, one capture pass on the 5090.

plausibly_competitive_unmeasured.why: Feature-identical to the artifact we benchmarked — NVFP4 W4A4 group 16, MTP bf16 wired into the index, vision tower bf16, 262,144 context, stock vLLM — but 2.65 GiB smaller, which is pure KV headroom on a 32 GB card. 19,932 downloads. It publishes throughput and nothing else.
plausibly_competitive_unmeasured.what_must_be_measured: v5 KLD and top-1, plus MTP acceptance rate. Also worth diffing its ignore list against unsloth's 303 entries to find out where the 2.65 GiB went.
plausibly_competitive_unmeasured.what_it_would_tell_us: Whether unsloth's extra 2.65 GiB (the group_0 FP8 attention/SSM/lm_head/last-8-MLP block) buys measurable fidelity or is dead weight. That is a direct, decidable question about the recipe we published against.

plausibly_competitive_unmeasured.why: The fastest-rising new-since-pin build: 21,015 downloads and 30 likes inside two days, on a card whose only quantisation-specific content is a version string and a link to a calibration set. It keeps the vision tower (333 tensors) and the MTP head (15 tensors) at 19.60 GiB, i.e. it sits in exactly our 32 GB envelope with our feature set, and it is calibrated on a STEM-and-agentic corpus rather than a generic one.
plausibly_competitive_unmeasured.what_must_be_measured: v5 KLD and top-1. Because the calibration corpus is agentic rather than generic, it is also the best available test of whether calibration-domain choice moves KLD on a general held-out suite — run it against our stratified breakdown (literary / code / encyclopedic / multilingual / scientific), not just the pooled mean.
plausibly_competitive_unmeasured.what_it_would_tell_us: Whether AWQ INT4 W4A16 with a task-shaped calibration set is competitive with NVFP4 at the same footprint, and whether calibration domain shows up as a stratum-level effect. It is also the clearest case in the landscape of adoption running far ahead of evidence — a measured number here has outsized public value.

plausibly_competitive_unmeasured.why: The closest methodological rival to our error-driven allocation work, and the only third party besides chriswritescode that publishes a KL protocol with a reproducibility hash. Their KL 0.0338 over 4,088 positions sits suspiciously close to our 0.031059 for unsloth NVFP4 over 10,480,640 positions — but the corpora are different, so the numbers are not comparable and must not be quoted side by side.
plausibly_competitive_unmeasured.what_must_be_measured: v5 KLD on identical contexts. Separately, re-score their published shipcard corpus through our harness to establish the cross-protocol offset, the same way chriswritescode established a +0.6% replay offset against us.
plausibly_competitive_unmeasured.what_it_would_tell_us: Whether per-Linear error pricing at 5.5 bpp beats our K5/K6 allocation at a comparable footprint, and how much of any gap is protocol rather than model. Also gives us a second, independent calibration of how much 4,088-position protocols understate variance.
plausibly_competitive_unmeasured.companion: rdtand/Qwen3.8-27B-PrismaAQUA-gridbook-12.1GiB-5080-vllm (revision bbbb4f53, 2026-08-16, 12.09 GiB) is the same allocator at a 16 GB target, but text-only and requiring the out-of-tree GridBook plugin — a different constraint, so a lower priority.

plausibly_competitive_unmeasured.why: Our own engine, uniform bitrate, vision and MTP preserved at every rung (MTP quantized to 4 bits). Already on the docs/29 attack list. Without it, every claim we make about non-uniform EXL3 allocation lacks its control arm.
plausibly_competitive_unmeasured.what_must_be_measured: v5 KLD at 5.00bpw (18.56 GiB, just under our context edition at 19.28 GiB) and at 6.00bpw (21.39 GiB, just under unsloth NVFP4 at 21.83 GiB). Two rungs, two matched footprints.
plausibly_competitive_unmeasured.what_it_would_tell_us: Exactly how much our K5/K6 allocation is worth versus uniform bitrate at the same bytes, in the same engine, with the same calibration family. This is the cleanest controlled comparison available anywhere in the landscape.

plausibly_competitive_unmeasured.why: First-party vendor builds from AMD, created after our baseline, that keep both the vision tower (333 tensors) and the MTP head (15 tensors) — a fact neither card mentions and which we established by reading the safetensors headers. At 18.5 GiB they are smaller than everything we ship. Their only evidence is GSM8K, where both report >100% recovery, which is the classic sign of a benchmark that cannot resolve the difference.
plausibly_competitive_unmeasured.what_must_be_measured: v5 KLD for both, plus whether the MTP head is loadable at all through Quark's config (the ignore list does not name it).
plausibly_competitive_unmeasured.what_it_would_tell_us: Whether Qronos (Hessian PTQ) and AWQ-MXFP4 land above or below NVFP4 at 4 bits, and it gives us the first vendor-produced comparison point that is not NVIDIA's format.

plausibly_competitive_unmeasured.why: A deliberately constructed memory ladder from a quanter with a track record, keeping vision (333 tensors) and bf16 MTP at every rung, from ~2.8 to ~4.5 bits. The cards state outright that evaluation is pending. Nobody has measured any of them.
plausibly_competitive_unmeasured.what_must_be_measured: v5 KLD at compact (13.12 GiB) and quality-MTP (17.90 GiB) — the two ends. Two points define the slope.
plausibly_competitive_unmeasured.what_it_would_tell_us: Where AutoRound INT ladders sit against our EXL3 ladder below 4 bits, in the region where our K4 (0.010604) is the only number we have.

plausibly_competitive_unmeasured.why: Not a 32 GB competitor — 29.83 GiB leaves no KV room — but it is the ONLY external artifact measured on our own suite, and it beats official FP8 by 36.6% on 136/136 contexts on v3 (0.008471 vs 0.013365, 278,392 positions). It already establishes a replay offset against us of +0.6% and a capture-environment floor of +0.000164 whose CI includes zero.
plausibly_competitive_unmeasured.what_must_be_measured: Re-run on v5 so it can be placed on the master KLD chart alongside our 0.002760 / 0.003210 / 0.003509 / 0.010604 and official FP8's 0.005294.
plausibly_competitive_unmeasured.what_it_would_tell_us: It converts a v3 result into a v5 result and, more importantly, it is a second independent validation of our harness by someone who is not us. That is worth more than the datapoint.

plausibly_competitive_unmeasured.why: 3.69 bpw GGUF that keeps the MTP draft head inside the file and ships a BF16 mmproj, built with explicit Gated-DeltaNet awareness (ssm_alpha / ssm_beta treated as first-class). 64 likes, the highest of any community GGUF with a stated objective. We already have a GGUF harness and a measured 0.000507 cross-engine floor.
plausibly_competitive_unmeasured.what_must_be_measured: v5 KLD on shard 0 through the existing GGUF path, against our Q8_0 0.001087 / Q6_K 0.002035 / UD-Q5_K_XL 0.004444 anchors.
plausibly_competitive_unmeasured.what_it_would_tell_us: Whether architecture-aware GGUF allocation beats unsloth's UD ladder at half the bytes — the GGUF-side analogue of our own allocation thesis.

measured_and_worse.finding: By its own published table, KLD 0.1267 against official FP8's 0.0523 on the same harness — i.e. 142% higher divergence weight-only, 27% higher as deployed. The card's prose says the opposite of its own numbers. At 28.87 GiB it is also outside the 32 GB envelope once KV is accounted for.
measured_and_worse.status: not a competitor on fidelity or footprint; still the best-documented MTP-preservation writeup in the landscape (84.0% draft acceptance, and the vLLM ignore-list failure mode where a mis-loaded bf16 head yields 0% acceptance while logging clean)

measured_and_worse.finding: WT2 PPL 7.4737 at 3.6165 bpw against IQ3_S 7.1820 at 3.6940 bpw — it loses to a stock GGUF quant at essentially the same bitrate, and the card publishes that fact.
measured_and_worse.status: research artifact, honestly reported, not a threat

long_context_specific_watchlist.assessment: Not a fidelity competitor — it is a repackaging of Avifenesh/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4-MTP-GGUF with patched metadata, and the card says so plainly. But it is the only artifact in the landscape that ships the official static-YaRN 1M recipe as a loadable default, and 1M KV at FP16 is ~61-64 GiB, so nobody is serving it on 32 GB. Worth watching, not worth measuring yet.

long_context_specific_watchlist.assessment: A 48 GB target, so it is not competing for our 32 GB slot; it is the closest thing to a long-context-first GGUF and a useful sanity check that F16 KV at 262k is achievable at all.

hard_failures.result: HTTP 404 'Invalid rev id' on /api/models/.../revision/<pin>; HTTP 500 on POST paths-info at the same rev
hard_failures.impact: none — the pin was recovered from our own archival mirror and cross-checked against tlwu's derived config

not_attempted_and_why.why: task constraint: metadata only. Byte counts come from the API sibling list; tensor names come from HTTP Range reads of the safetensors JSON header (first 8 bytes for the length, then the header itself).

not_attempted_and_why.target: GGUF internal metadata (per-tensor ggml types, KV blocks)
not_attempted_and_why.why: reading it means range-reading each .gguf header across 240+ GGUF repos; classification for those relies on filenames and cards. This is the largest single blind spot in the scan.
not_attempted_and_why.consequence: for GGUF repos, statements about which tensors are quantised how are card claims, not verified facts — except where the card itself publishes the mix (empero-ai Ridge, AlexanderKyng, enginetown).

not_attempted_and_why.why: the RTX 5090 is held by KvDtypeSweep and the rental must stay free. Every fidelity number in this document is somebody else's published number or one of ours from a prior receipt; none was produced by this scan.

coverage_caveats.issue: HF full-text search is fuzzy and token-based
coverage_caveats.mitigation: instead of trusting it, every one of the 952 candidate model cards was fetched and regex-scanned for 'malaiwah', 'qwen38-27b-fidelity-suite', 'qwen38-27b-exl3', 'K5K6' and 'gilded-gnosis'. The full-text endpoint returned 79 apparent external hits for a loose 'Qwen3.8-27B-K4' query; direct card scanning reduced that to exactly one genuine citation.
coverage_caveats.residual_risk: a card that credits us only inside an embedded image, or via a bare URL we did not pattern-match, would still be missed.

coverage_caveats.detail: 17 repos have usedStorage far above their HEAD byte count. Only two actually keep content on non-main branches: turboderp/Qwen3.8-27B-exl3 (7 bitrate branches, fully inventoried here) and Minachist/Qwen3.8-27B-INT8-AutoRound (main, main-gs128, linear-attn-bf16, linear-attn-bf16-gs128 — inventoried at HEAD only). For the other 15 the excess is superseded revisions.
coverage_caveats.residual_risk: Minachist's three non-main branches were not inventoried.

coverage_caveats.detail: 464 of 952 candidates got full detail (metadata + card + config.json + weight index). The 488 not detailed are, by construction, low-traction repos created before the cutoff or with no focus format — but each still had its card fetched and scanned.
coverage_caveats.residual_risk: a well-argued objective inside a zero-download repo with a non-focus format would be summarised only from its name and tags.

coverage_caveats.detail: 126 sibling shard repos collapsed to one representative. They are a per-tensor shard library, not 126 opinions.
coverage_caveats.residual_risk: none material; it does inflate any raw repo count by ~13%.

coverage_caveats.detail: HF reports a 30-day rolling figure. Every count here is as of the scan timestamp and will drift.
